event.summary: Retiring old terminal probes and safeguards is intentional for ended tmux terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Old terminal screens and programs no longer survive the upgrade, and a failure to end their server can allow a later Restart to start another agent. Could-be-highest: yes; ending user processes and terminal history is loss of user-owned work, and the deleted live-pane/no-pid and unusable-server safeguards formerly prevented unsafe restart assumptions. Suggested bucket: highest if unintended; proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance, pending independent check. SPEC.md:3003–3016 says: ‘This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.’ It also says: ‘A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.’ SPEC_impl.md:2888–2889 says: ‘The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone: what remains is the startup step that ends them (below), and the installation’s tmux policy after it.’ Assigned patch lines 11–89 delete the old pane process parser and lines 938–996 delete unusable-server guards; removing these old-driver paths accords with those contracts. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance, source-only; still check startup ordering and replacement callers before closing the pass. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this acceptance covers ending old terminals and the stated failure residual, not harm to terminal-host sessions or unrelated processes.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing the exact-boolean tmux paste-mode parser would permit a multi-line prompt to reach a shell as commands. Could-be-highest: yes, if that deletion removed the effective prompt-delivery safety gate. Suggested bucket: highest for that suspected security route, but source refutes the route. Confidence: confirmed source-only refutation. proposed_drop: the parser and its test served the retired tmux driver; the retained host-only delivery path in crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:11944–12010 requires a live terminal, accepted agent status, caught-up replay at 11999–12005, and terminal.modes().bracketed_paste at 12007–12009 before deliver_prompt_to_host. It forms one bracketed paste at 11987–11991; validation excludes ESC as documented at 11992. The assigned patch deletes the tmux-only parser and its exact-boolean fixture at patch lines 118–156, while source keeps an independent host-mode gate. This is not evidence that every paste race is impossible; it settles the specific deletion concern. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Deleted tmux paste-mode parser does not remove the host prompt-delivery gate
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR, original wording preserved: Considered whether removing the exact-boolean tmux paste-mode parser would permit a multi-line prompt to reach a shell as commands. Original suspected consequence: unintended command execution, potentially highest. Could-be-highest: yes if a shipped delivery route lost its safety gate; no such route is established here. Suggested bucket: highest for the original suspected security consequence; proposed_drop remains a proposal, based on source refutation rather than reduced impact or rarity. Confidence: confirmed source-only refutation of the specific deletion and test-sensitivity concern. Production: service/core.rs:11944–12010 requires live terminal evidence, accepted activity, replay caught_up and modes().bracketed_paste before forming/sending the bracketed paste. The old parser's unexpanded or malformed tmux string inputs no longer exist: host modes are typed booleans from the terminal emulator. SPEC_impl.md:2225–2228 requires that host gate. SPEC.md:3892–3895 additionally states the cross-agent prompt verb is disabled before shipment; this is secondary to the retained gate, not a substitute for testing it. Synthesis checks of surviving tests: core/tests/host_terminals.rs:541–589 creates an idle running Claude target, attempts a multiline prompt with mode off, requires the specific off-mode refusal and zero received bytes, enables mode and waits for it, then requires exact bracketed bytes and submit for small and multi-frame capped prompts. Removing the gate would fail its refusal assertion; indiscriminately refusing would fail its later success assertions. The retained real-host test core.rs:20110–20121 also requires off-mode refusal before any recorded input. host_terminals.rs:1484–1535 deliberately exposes paste mode on while caught_up is false, requires the specific replay refusal and no bytes, then finishes replay and requires delivery, so omitting only the replay gate is distinguishable too. These are source-derived sensitivity conclusions; no mutation experiment or test execution was performed. Therefore the deleted exact-string parser test has no surviving string-parser responsibility to exercise, while actual host safety gates still have distinguishing tests. Caveat: this refutes neither every paste race nor risks of future re-enablement. possible_cover: none known; no queue or coverage metadata searched. No drop accepted; preserve for caller independent check.

event.summary: Version ordering and exact parsing coverage survives the driver retirement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether moving the version-policy tests during driver deletion weakened the installation's version acceptance checks. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this test movement; suggested bucket: other if coverage had regressed. Confidence: confirmed source-only refutation. proposed_drop: both assigned added tests are preserved verbatim from the parent revision's tmux.rs:5848–5947 (the ordering test and the whole-line parsing/refusal test). Current source tmux.rs:677–685 distinguishes patch letters and numeric minors, and 695–757 checks round-trip and exact framing refusals; these agree with SPEC_impl.md:2957–2960: "Versions above the floor are accepted in tmux's own release spelling (`major.minor` plus at most one patch letter); a version newer than the pinned one earns a one-time warning that it is unaudited, never a refusal. Anything the parser cannot read exactly — `next-3.8`, release candidates, distro-decorated strings — is refused rather than guessed about: a version Farhelm cannot name is one nobody audited it against." Reviewed the changed tests against the supplied test-authoring checklist; the assertions use pure parsing and do not depend on external fixture readiness or mutate process environment. possible_cover: none. No runtime tests or reproductions performed.

Startup/readoption/record settling match session and tab through names_tab at 1476–1478 and 1136–1150, and install checks cell/old-runtime identity at 1183–1198. Its 1270–1295 cross-session record fixture requires a running foreign child both before and after unconditional Delete, no writes and row retention. Its 3703–3780 adopts a tab host, removes its socket while the adopted process remains this test runner, requires close refusal, and checks failed-end retry state plus retained record. Removing those guards would contradict those assertions; no mutation experiment was performed. The obsolete tmux tests' string-format and recycled-pane cases have no surviving parser responsibility, while host identity remains checked at its actual boundaries. possible_cover: none known; no coverage sources searched.
